```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sudarsono_2026_ganciclovir_hfim"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sudarsono_2026_ganciclovir_hfim"))$description`
* Article: [Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2026;70(8):e00381-26](https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00381-26)

Sudarsono and colleagues built a low-cost hollow-fiber infection model (HFIM)
for antiviral PK/PD studies of cytomegalovirus (CMV). A hemodialyzer cartridge
holds CMV-infected MRC-5 human lung fibroblasts in its extra-capillary space,
connected to a 0.2 L central reservoir. Ganciclovir was infused into the
reservoir (2 mg over 1 h, i.e. 2 mg/h, every 12 h), and drug-free medium was
pumped in with matched outflow to waste to mimic clearance and reproduce a
human-like plasma concentration-time profile. Concentrations sampled from the
intracapillary space were fitted with a one-compartment model in nlmixr2
(Table 1). The packaged model reproduces that one-compartment system; the
descriptive virology (Figures 2 and 5) is not modelled.

# Population

The "population" is the hollow-fiber system itself rather than a set of
subjects. Two independent experiments provided the ganciclovir concentrations
used for the one-compartment fit (Figure 3). MRC-5 cells (5.0e7) were inoculated
into the cartridge together with CMV (the lab-adapted Towne strain at MOI 0.1 or
the BAC-derived wild-type-like Merlin strain at MOI 0.01) and cultured at
37 degrees C with 5% CO2. The main circulation loop ran at 30 mL/min to keep the
cartridge and reservoir concentrations equilibrated, which Figure 4 confirms.

The same information is available programmatically via the model's `population`
metadata (`readModelDb("Sudarsono_2026_ganciclovir_hfim")()$population`).

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Sudarsono_2026_ganciclovir_hfim.R`. The
table below collects them in one place for review.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL)           | 0.033 L/h | Table 1, row 'Clearance (L/h)', estimate 0.033 (0.2 %RSE) |
| `lvc` (Vc)           | 0.3 L | Table 1, row 'Volume of distribution (L)', estimate 0.3 (2.05 %RSE) |
| `kel = cl / vc`      | 0.11 1/h | Table 1, row 'Elimination rate constant (h-1)', estimate 0.11 (0.033 / 0.3 = 0.11) |
| `d/dt(central)`      | n/a | One-compartment model, Methods 'PK analysis'; design Eqs 1-3 |
| AUC0-12 (validation target) | 42.2 mg*h/L | Table 1, row 'AUC0-12 (mg.h/L)' |

The elimination rate constant is a derived micro-constant (`kel = cl / vc`), not
an independent parameter: `0.033 / 0.3 = 0.11 1/h`, matching the Table 1
estimate.

# Virtual cohort

The model carries no between-experiment variability and no residual-error term
(the paper reports point estimates only), so the simulation is a single
deterministic typical-value profile. The dosing regimen is the one used in the
HFIM: ganciclovir 2 mg infused over 1 h every 12 h.

```{r cohort}
# Single first dose for the NCA comparison (AUC0-12 is a first-interval
# quantity in the paper). amt = 2 mg infused over dur = 1 h into central.
dose_single <- rxode2::et(amt = 2, dur = 1, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05)) |>
  as.data.frame()
dose_single$regimen <- "ganciclovir 2 mg"

# Multi-dose profile for the Figure 3 replication: q12h for 3 days (6 doses).
dose_multi <- rxode2::et(amt = 2, dur = 1, cmt = "central", ii = 12, addl = 5) |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 72, by = 0.1)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Sudarsono_2026_ganciclovir_hfim")

sim_single <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = dose_single, keep = "regimen") |>
  as.data.frame()
sim_multi <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = dose_multi) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-3, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
# Replicates Figure 3 of Sudarsono 2026: the simulated ganciclovir
# concentration-time profile (2 mg, 1-h infusion, q12h) over three days.
ggplot(sim_multi, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "navy", linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Ganciclovir (mg/L)",
    title = "Figure 3 - simulated ganciclovir profile in the HFIM",
    caption = "Replicates the simulated line of Figure 3 of Sudarsono 2026."
  )
```

The simulated profile shows the sawtooth of a 1-h infusion every 12 h, peaking
near 8 mg/L at the end of each infusion and declining toward a ~2 mg/L trough,
in agreement with the observed data points of Figure 3 and the mean cartridge
profile of Figure 4B.

# PKNCA validation

The one quantitative exposure metric the paper reports is AUC0-12 = 42.2
mg*h/L. The block below computes it from the simulated first-dose profile over
the 0-12 h interval.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_single |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, regimen)

# Guarantee a time = 0 row (Cc = 0 pre-dose for an infusion start).
sim_nca <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> dplyr::distinct(id, regimen) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, regimen, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, regimen, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)

dose_df <- dose_single |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, regimen)

dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 12,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)

nca_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(nca_data)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,            ~auclast,
  "ganciclovir 2 mg",  42.2
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "regimen",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)

knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. published ganciclovir AUC0-12. * differs from reference by >20%."
)
```

The simulated AUC0-12 reproduces the published 42.2 mg*h/L, confirming that the
packaged one-compartment parameters match the paper's fit.

# Assumptions and deviations

- The paper reports typical-value estimates only (no between-experiment
  variability, no residual-error structure), so the model carries no random
  effects; the simulation is deterministic.
- The fitted volume of distribution (0.3 L) exceeds the nominal reservoir volume
  (0.2 L) that the pump settings were designed around; the maintainers kept the
  fitted estimate, which presumably absorbs the cartridge and tubing volumes.
- `kel` is encoded as the derived micro-constant `cl / vc` (0.11 1/h), matching
  the Table 1 estimate rather than being estimated independently.
- Cmax and Tmax are computed for completeness but are not compared against the
  paper, which tabulated only CL, Vc, Ke and AUC0-12; the design target Cmax of
  10 mg/L used the input (not fitted) parameters.
- The CMV replication data (Figures 2 and 5, Figures S1-S2) are descriptive;
  the authors fitted no pharmacodynamic model, so none is packaged.
- No correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-11-16.
